text.p: The inflationary expectations of Australian consumers for the upcoming year showed a small decline in March, the Melbourne Institute said on Thursday. The March reading of 3.5 percent, down from 3.7 percent in February, is the equal lowest recorded values since July 1994.
"Presumably consumers are lowering their inflationary expectations as news of the recent falls in inflation filters through the economy," the Institute said.
However the survey found consumers' median notion of current inflation was 2.6 percent, well above the actual consumer price index for the year to December of 1.5 percent.
"Moreover, many consumers are expecting negligible real wage increases, as just over half of the employed respondents expected no pay rise or pay cuts over the next 12 months," the Institute said.
Males had the lowest inflationary expectations, at 3.1 percent, compared with 4.6 percent for females.
Those in employment had lower inflationary expectations, with white collar workers having lower expectations than blue collar workers.
Inflation expectations of people with university eductation were lower than those who had left school before matriculation, the survey found.
